source.title: A Geometric Analysis of Neural Collapse with Unconstrained Features
source.authors: Zhi-Hui Zhu; Tian-Yu Ding; Jin-Xin Zhou; Xiao Li; Chong You; Jeremias Sulam; Qing Qu

record.file_problem: Text contains the full paper, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports CIFAR-10 training-error outcomes under width variation and random labels, bearing on whether training can fit the training set.
record.gate_note: Only the random-label CIFAR-10 training-error findings in Section 4.2 are extracted. Neural-collapse metrics, test accuracy, and results cited from other work do not directly measure a listed version's training-error outcome.
record.test_reason: Section 4.2 measures training misclassification on randomly labeled CIFAR-10 using convolutional ResNet18 networks trained with SGD, matching V1's method and outcome. The study is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the random-label experiment but omits the paper's main conclusion: under its unconstrained-feature assumptions, global minimizers exhibit neural collapse and other critical points are strict saddles. Experiments support neural collapse across optimizers and motivate fixed classifiers and reduced feature dimensions. The authors explicitly caution that this analysis assumes successful optimization of the preceding network layers and does not explain generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies neural collapse and its optimization landscape; the random-label experiments use CIFAR10 training with width sweeps, rather than a direct replication of the listed studies' recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Width affects the reported training error: larger networks tend to achieve smaller error.

fits_no_version.finding: Sufficiently large four-layer MLPs memorize random CIFAR-10 labels with zero training error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sufficiently wide fully connected networks trained with SGD can fit completely random CIFAR-10 labels.

fits_no_version.finding: The regularized cross-entropy unconstrained-feature model has no spurious local minima under the stated balanced-class and feature-dimension assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A simplified model optimizing features and classifiers directly has a benign optimization landscape; this does not establish V2's ReLU teacher-student result.

record.problems: The text gives no exact width threshold or numerical training-error values for the zero-error result; those values appear only in Figure 5. Initialization is not specified for these experiments.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 4 shows training and test accuracy for ResNet18 on MNIST and CIFAR10 across optimizers, but the text does not state exact training-error results and the plotted values are figure-only; Figure 6 and Figure 7 report neural-collapse metrics or accuracy rather than a separate textual training-error finding relevant to the listed versions.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100, partially corrupted labels, random-label training with Adam, and controlled effects of early stopping or regularization. Random initialization is not documented. Width-specific outcomes cannot be read from the supplied figure text.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization and the effect of one or two extra student neurons on spurious-minimum frequency.
Depth-dependent degradation and comparisons between plain networks, identity shortcuts, special tanh initialization, or Fixup.
Comparative initialization effects on training speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss transients, curvature evolution, and divergence.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization or with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's limits_scope label: width dependence is already allowed by V1, and an unspecified threshold is an evidence-resolution limitation rather than a contradictory result. Figures 4 and 7 are already declared in rows_left_out, so they do not require missing entries. Neural-collapse metrics alone do not measure any listed claim version.
